original_requirement.heading: Work packages
original_requirement.text: Implement optional SQLite persistence, leases, owner isolation, trajectories and journals; restart/crash-window and owner-isolation fixtures pass against both runtimes.

audit_method: Read existing Source/native code and actual host/Linux full test JSON events; verify selected file hashes against the final current-runtime manifest and raw logs against terminal receipts. No tests, builds, captures or containers launched. Original ledger preserved unchanged; only this final private JSON appended.
scope: The seven recipe groups explicitly requested by the original-acceptance review: manager7, cron/scheduled, lease/rollback, killed-generation, compaction3, decision2 and team restart. This does not apply status changes to the344-row audit.

groups.title: Manager reconstruction, owner isolation and interrupted transcript repair

recipe_inventory.native_additional: publicly created session close/reopen and resumed turn

assertions: Native Store closes before successor Manager construction; compares durable owner, identity, creation time, run count, workspace and transcript/epoch repair.
Foreign owner cannot read restored session; live foreign lease prevents repair and Run/provider execution until released; duplicate restore is empty.
Tools recipe expires pending approvals with resolution metadata; second reopen retains repair; Stop releases owned lease.
Resumed actual provider sees persisted transcript prefix plus queued steering; CatchUpEvents keeps increasing scoped sequence above saved payload sequence9.
boundaries: Source uses two real Managers over an actual SQLite store, but does not close/reopen that store between those two Managers; native adds database reopening.

Native preservation of saved todos/steering and monotonic public event sequence are documented adaptations to Source metadata-loss/payload-sequence reset behavior; not every Source field is compared as literal equality.
Process reconstruction and seeded interrupted histories; no claim that all crash or external-effect windows are captured.
groups.source_native_relationship: Direct consumer of all seven actual Source recipes, plus native database-close/reopen strengthening.

groups.title: Scheduled restoration and durable operator arming

recipe_inventory.native_composition: persist schedule, Stop/close/reopen, explicit arm+tick, resumed turn, third reopen

assertions: Scheduled recipes compare bound versus current factory workspace, current SystemBuilder, owner/mode/run/status/history, repeated restoration identity, persisted repair and metadata.
Missing SQL session is not recreated; foreign/missing SQL paths invoke no provider; no-store missing session has its explicit ephemeral behavior.

Native Cron Start restores definitions disarmed and does not eagerly restore session; pre-arm tick has no model call; explicit arm+tick lazily restores and checks SQL flush before actual provider request.
One-shot is removed before resolution; failed claim/save never dispatches; persisted disk copy is masked; dispatch uses fresh untrusted authority with no ActorID/capabilities.
After Stop/reopen the run count is2 and one-shot remains absent; owner isolation and lease release are asserted.
boundaries: Source cron lifecycle uses Recording._fire rather than an actual model; native Manager/SQLite composition supplies a separate real execution bridge.
Cron definition JSON and local claim files are distinct from SQLite session/history/lease persistence.
Controlled local civil-minute ticks and explicit operator arming; no new clock-drift, power-loss or external-effect atomicity assertion.
groups.source_native_relationship: Direct scheduled7 and scheduler lifecycle fixture comparisons plus native combined Manager/SQLite/cron restart test.

groups.title: Lease ownership, atomic transcript/delete rollback and reservation release

rollback_windows: session delete abort after earlier deletes

assertions: Two SQLite connections replay13 explicit-clock Source acquire/renew/release/expiry steps; missing session cannot claim, metadata upsert cannot transfer/release lease, and reopen retains holder.
Twenty real concurrent two-connection claim trials require exactly one winner and matching holder; cancelled/closed calls fail.
Actual SQLite trigger aborts second transcript insert; no partial batch survives and exact current/old epochs remain after close/reopen.
Actual BEFORE DELETE trigger aborts session deletion: earlier message/event deletion rolls back; successful deletion retains action/approval audit rows, including after reopen.
Cancellation before commit rolls back inserted row and releases writer reservation for another connection.
Actual second action-update abort leaves both inflight actions unchanged; missing/closed handling is explicit.
boundaries: Clock-controlled lease fixture is not a naturally elapsed crash process; the killed-generation group provides that distinct observation.
Cancellation and second action-update rollback are native strengthenings, not claimed as rows in the same exported Source fixture.
Lease exclusion does not fence an external effect; finite transaction profiles are not a universal concurrent or disk-failure certificate.
groups.source_native_relationship: Direct Source lease/transcript/delete fixtures with separately identified native concurrency/cancellation/recovery rollback controls.

groups.title: Owned process death during admitted generation and natural lease expiry
assertions: Dedicated owned child validates actual provider request only after SQL transcript flush and lease publication; atomic checkpoint PID must match exact child and differ from parent.
Parent kills and joins only owned writer without Manager.Stop or Store.Close; persisted unexpired lease remains.
Restoration exposes owner-bound pending handle with unanswered history; premature Run returns lease lost and provider call count0.
After natural8s expiry, Run repairs interrupted turn, installs different lease owner, sends exact interrupted-generation marker to actual provider, and persists resumed turn.
Second database reopen retains repair/history and run_count2; helper is skipped in the main test process and is not counted as an independent passing top-level test.
boundaries: No paired actual Python SIGKILL producer or identical cross-language process-kill fixture is asserted by this ledger; Source seeded-repair and expiry evidence are linked separately.
The additional native kill recipe covers the admitted-generation window on executed OS; no power-loss, arbitrary in-flight transaction kill or external-effect reconciliation claim.
groups.source_native_relationship: Native process-kill strengthening of Source seeded interrupted-history/lease contracts; not a direct common subprocess fixture.

groups.title: Complete tool-batch archive and compaction/SQLite restart composition
assertions: Source summary fixture records actual DefaultCompactor.compact archive bytes, output history, summary request and provenance; Go compares these exactly after workspace normalization.
Native restart composition executes compress+read_file together and requires archive to contain whole paired three-message batch including later read result.
Success stores summary in epoch2 and retains paired epoch1; provenance is tied to pre-rewrite epoch1/archive with replaced-message count3 and metered summary input.
Failure/cancellation writes archive but preserves canonical paired epoch1 and emits no successful-summary receipt.
Database close/reopen preserves exact identity/history/current+historical epoch/event prefix; next provider receives retained prefix; lease health and archive bytes remain intact.
boundaries: Three native restart compositions are not three exported end-to-end Source recipes; only summary primitive is directly fixture-matched, with Source unit/integration evidence for mirroring, restart and cancellation.
Source test named recovery_needs_only_the_durable_log constructs a second Manager in the same Python process and manually releases lease; it is not proof of a second OS process.
Manual forced summary failure differs from automatic maybe_compact failure handling; the native tests name and assert those paths separately.
Small paired history proof; no arbitrary-size compaction or every archival profile claim.
groups.source_native_relationship: Actual Source summary fixture comparison plus bounded independent native three-outcome real-SQL composition.

groups.title: Large settled decision replay after SQLite reopen with current permission
assertions: Actual Source decision gate closes/reopens SQLite and replays same action; native managed tool path compares retained byte length, canonical SHA256, exact replay and backend calls1.
New Manager restores exact archived transcript but permission is interactive rather than restored auto authority.
Current operator must explicitly choose auto before same RunContext/tool-use replay; later readonly retry cannot expose cached result and cannot call backend.
Replay/denial leave settled action unchanged; final transcript pairing and lease health are asserted.
boundaries: Source replay fixture exercises actual tool gate/journal, native adds Manager restoration and current-authority checks.
Explicit inert high-threshold compactor preserves the large payload; default compaction is covered separately.
Aggregate shedding is Source in-memory journal scope, not a newly claimed durable aggregate policy.
groups.source_native_relationship: Direct consumer of both actual sqlite-reopen Source result recipes plus native managed-restart/current-authority strengthening.

groups.title: Teammate history reconstruction, independent team identity and resumed turn
assertions: Source uses real SQLite Store and SessionManager, spawns actual teammate initial turn, queues old-team mail, stops/closes and constructs fresh managers twice.

Native matches selected typed first/second reopen observations: two restored sessions, owner/workspace, independent team identity/name, interactive mode, idle status/run count/history and old/new inbox counts.
First restoration invokes no extra model; resumed explicit turn invokes exactly one model and matches request prefix, recursive-spawn visibility, result/history and run_count2.
Second restoration again invokes no model and retains the resumed history and pending old-team mailbox.
boundaries: Consumer projection does not directly compare Source label, role_present, tasks_present, runner_present or old_roster_present fields; do not call the entire exported restart object exact equality.
Native Manager defaults and Source explicit injectors=[] differ in assembly; this recipe keeps old mail under the old team key and new inbox empty, so no notification injection is asserted.
groups.source_native_relationship: Direct actual Source two-reopen recipe, compared through explicit typed observation subsets and actual resumed provider request.

explicit_remaining_work.action: Completed binding at current runtime: corrected Linux full and race each contain the same25 top-level and49 subtest pass names as the host stages; final Source/full/vet/race result hashes match the final24-gate receipt. Historical first failure/manual stop remain separate and do not count as passes.

explicit_remaining_work.fact: Killed-generation is an additional native OS-process test; compaction3 is native composition plus actual Source primitive/unit evidence. No shared end-to-end Source fixture is claimed for those full combinations, and no extra power-loss requirement is invented.

The named persistence recipe queue has current host execution links; this ledger is not a standalone certificate for every trajectory/journal/owner operation or full original G5/G7 acceptance. Root must reconcile it with existing broader original acceptance evidence, not infer missing runtime features from historical pending prose.

historical_linux_attempts.interpretation: The initial complete Linux race cohort failed one background message-phase assertion (5 versus Source4). Its native consumer used nil injectors, selecting default background/team injection although the Source recipe disabled those injectors. The fourth commit corrects only that test to explicit empty injectors with absence assertions; expected4 messages and task outcomes are preserved. This is a consumer assembly correction, not a production fix or universal timing reliability proof.
Manual SIGTERM after the identified consumer assembly mismatch; not a passed cohort, OOM or observed host-pressure failure. No final cgroup sample was published.

limitations: NORMAL SQLite synchronization is not power-loss durability.
Lease exclusion is not external-effect fencing.
No new arbitrary SQL transaction-kill or exhaustive malformed archive/concurrency standard is added.
Source full pytest output is aggregate; source recipe assertions are statically linked and included by the full-suite command, not falsely presented as per-test machine events.
